cards.text: Book of Judges, friend: "Again the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD," so He delivers them into an enemy's hand for forty years. AGAIN, like me hitting snooze for the fifth time and acting shocked I'm late.

cards.question: Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD again. Who does He deliver them into the hand of?

cards.text: Now meet Manoah, a man from Zorah, from the clan of the Danites. His wife was barren and had no children, and that's right where this story starts.
Then the angel of the LORD shows up. Not to Manoah. To his wife.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah's wife it is true she is barren. Then what does he tell her?

answers.text: She will give birth to a son
She will give birth to twins
She will give birth to a daughter

cards.text: And he's not done. "Now please be careful," he says, and he gives her things to stay away from, starting right now.

cards.question: The angel tells Manoah's wife not to drink wine or strong drink, and not to eat anything ___.

cards.text: Then the angel gets specific about the boy: "And no razor shall touch his head," he says. No razor, friend. My mustache just stood up and applauded.

cards.question: No razor will touch the boy's head. What does the angel say the boy will be to God from the womb?
The angel says the boy will finish the deliverance of Israel from the hand of the Philistines.

cards.text: So the woman goes and tells her husband a man of God came to her. She says his appearance was like the angel of God, "exceedingly awesome."

cards.question: Manoah's wife tells him she asked the man of God where he came from.
Manoah's wife repeats the message to him. How long does she say the boy will be a Nazirite to God?

answers.text: From the womb until his death
From the womb until he is grown
From his birth until he marries

cards.text: Then Manoah prays to the LORD. Some of us would've hit the group chat first, friend, but Manoah takes it right to the top.

cards.question: Manoah hears his wife's news and prays to the LORD. What does he ask for?

answers.text: That the man of God would come again to teach them
That the LORD would give them a sign first
That the boy would be born very soon

cards.text: "And God listened to the voice of Manoah," and the angel of God comes back to the woman while she's sitting in the field.

cards.question: When the angel of God returns, Manoah is in the field with his wife.

cards.text: She runs quickly to tell her husband the man is back. Manoah prayed for this visit and wasn't even in the field for it, like waiting all day on a delivery, stepping away for ONE minute, and hearing the doorbell from the other room.
So Manoah got up and followed his wife. He walks right up and asks, "Are you the man who spoke to my wife?"

cards.question: The man tells Manoah he is the one who spoke to his wife.

cards.text: Then Manoah asks, "When your words come to pass, what will be the boy’s rule of life and mission?" I spent years in a junk drawer next to a pile of old instruction manuals, friend, and Manoah would've read EVERY one.

cards.question: Manoah asks about the boy's rule of life and mission. How does the angel of the LORD answer?

answers.text: His wife must do all the angel told her
Manoah must take the boy to the priests
Manoah must teach the boy to fight

cards.question: The angel adds that Manoah's wife must not eat anything that comes from the vine.

cards.text: "Please stay here," Manoah says, so they can prepare a young goat for him. This man is NOT letting a guest leave without feeding him.

cards.question: Manoah offers to prepare a young goat for the angel of the LORD. What does the angel say?

answers.text: He won't eat but they may offer it to the LORD
He will stay and eat it with them gladly
They should save it for the boy's birth

cards.text: Manoah did not know that it was the angel of the LORD. Then he asks for a name, so they can honor him when his word comes to pass.

cards.question: The angel of the LORD tells Manoah his name.

cards.text: Instead he asks, "Why do you ask my name," and says it's beyond comprehension.
Then Manoah offers a young goat and a grain offering on a rock to the LORD. As Manoah and his wife look on, "the LORD did a marvelous thing."

cards.question: When the flame goes up from the altar to the sky, the angel of the LORD ___ in the flame.
When Manoah and his wife see the angel go up in the flame, they run from the altar.

cards.text: The angel of the LORD doesn't appear to them again, and "Manoah realized that it had been the angel of the LORD." That's like chatting with a guy for ten minutes, he walks off, and THEN it hits you: that was the new boss.

cards.question: Manoah tells his wife they are going to ___, because they have seen God.
Manoah is sure they're going to die. What reason does his wife give that they won't?

answers.text: The angel promised them long life
They obeyed every rule he gave

cards.text: I bet Manoah's heart is pounding, but his wife comes with receipts: the LORD wouldn't have shown them all these things or spoken to them this way. She didn't bring an argument, friend, she brought a whole case file.
So the woman gives birth to a son and names him Samson, and somewhere a barber just sighed. "The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him."

cards.question: As Samson grows, something begins to stir him at Mahaneh-dan. What is it?

cards.text: Right there at Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol. Keep your apron on, friend, because the oven on Samson's story is only just warming up.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the angel's arrival, "Not to Manoah." and "To his wife." That exceeds the two-sentence limit.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The earlier cards give no basis for reasoning out "unclean" rather than "sweet" or "cooked." The blank therefore asks for wording the baker has not seen instead of an inferable meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the razor statement, "No razor, friend." and the mustache reaction. It needs to be compressed to one or two sentences.

findings.problem: Too much of this stop depends on luck rather than informed picks. Cards 10, 12 and 17 are unsupported true-or-false coin flips, while cards 2, 5, 7, 9 and 13 also ask for details that cannot be reasoned from the earlier cards. This goes beyond a few discovery questions.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer. A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: The preceding card says only that Manoah realized who the visitor had been. It gives no basis for choosing "die" over the other completions, so this blank tests unseen wording rather than a meaning the baker can reason out.
